advices.diagnosis: The class has a very low cohesion (LCOM4 = 4) because each accessor method only touches a single private attribute, resulting in four disconnected components. It is a pure data holder (DAM = 1.0, DCC = 0) with no behavior beyond a simple tier check, which matches the "data_class" smell label. While the high LCOM4 is expected for a data class, the metrics suggest the class could gain cohesion by adding domain‑relevant behavior that operates on multiple attributes.

suggestions.title: Introduce domain behavior to improve cohesion
suggestions.sketch:
Add methods that combine attributes, e.g.:
```python
    def upgrade_to_premium(self) -> None:
        self._tier = "premium"

    def display_name(self) -> str:
        return f"{self._name} <{self._email}>"
```
These methods reference more than one attribute, creating connections between previously isolated accessor methods and thus reducing LCOM4. No new external classes are required, but if a dedicated Tier value object is introduced later, DCC would increase.

advices.risk_notes: Adding behavior changes the class's responsibility from a pure DTO to a richer domain entity; existing code that treats Customer as a simple data container may need to be updated. If the new methods are not used, the metric improvement is only theoretical. Introducing a Tier value object would increase DCC and add import considerations, so weigh the benefit of stronger type safety against the added coupling.
